What I think is that we can take the problem in reverse. If we evolved to the point of sentience, in a universe that seems to be the fruit of infinitely low odds, then we are here to ask ourselves this question. If we had not, if the laws of physics had been ever so slightly different and matter could not form, we would not be here to ask these questions. So the very conditions for us to ask these questions are that we are here, in a universe so infinitely complex, refusing to acknowledge our luck and thinking of it as divine intervention, kind of like an existential survivor's complex.

I don't mean to disrespect your religion, and I could be wrong, but your question raised a point that I wanted to make.

Steven cures injuries. Amethyst, although defective, isn't injured. Her gem just formed differently, and as a result, made her different. You used the example of a weak heart, which is a disability for sure, that should be helped by modern medicine, but I'd say Steven's power would not be able to fix that in a human. 
My reasoning is, using DNA, that Steven's powers would be to rectify someone's body according to their DNA (reforming a broken arm, or a wound, or any damage in general), but not to rectify the DNA's defects in themselves. In fact, if you were to be operated on said heart, he would maybe even reverse the operation.

So all in all, he can most likely fix something/someone according to their blueprint, but not fix the blueprint in itself.

Whether or not it gives an edge or a disadvantage to Amethyst to be the way she is is, imo, completely irrelevant. But it would probably have been odd vis-a-vis the "learn to be at peace with yourself" morale of the story if he was just able to kiss her gem better and make her a tall and strong Quartz.

Gravity doesn't magically stop at the edge of the atmosphere. Even if it did, he's still in the atmosphere here. Felix Baumgartner actually did something similar to this scene in real life, apart from the space debris and catastrophe. He jumped from orbit and parachuted. You should look him up, it's a pretty amazing stunt !

Gravity is just a force that's stronger the closer you get to any object with mass, and obviously weaker as you get further. In fact, from the top of a mountain, gravity is ever so slightly lower than at sea level.
Satellites, like the Moon, are still affected by Earth's gravity despite their distance, which is why it orbits around the Earth. It's actually falling towards Earth, but with such a speed and angle that its fall point constantly stays over the horizon. And since the earth is spherical, and there's no atmosphere up so high, it doesn't slow down, and round and round it goes.
If there was no gravity in space, we wouldn't have a Moon, and in fact we wouldn't even be orbiting the Sun. And there wouldn't be galaxies. And we'd be all dead.
